title: Engineering Competing Fractional Topological States in a BHZ Superlattice
abstract: Scalar superlattices offer a route from simple topological bands to fractionalized states, while multicomponent systems raise the additional question of which fractional order is energetically selected. We show that a scalar superlattice applied to the Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) Chern-insulator model produces an isolated C = +1 miniband with strongly improved Berry-curvature and quantum metric uniformity. Exact diagonalization of the projected interaction identifies a 1/3 fractional Chern insulator in this miniband. Restoring the time-reversed partner to form the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) superlattice yields, at total filling 2/3, a balanced fractional quantum spin Hall (FQSH)-like state and a fully polarized 2/3 fractional Chern insulator. Their competition separates two aspects of fractional-state control: the finite-momentum intercomponent coupling governs the stability of the balanced FQSH-like state, whereas a uniform pseudospin anisotropy shifts the relative energies of conserved sectors and can switch the global ground state between the balanced and polarized states. These results establish a minimal lattice setting that connects topological-miniband reconstruction, fractional-state formation, and fractional-state selection, illustrating how distinct levels of control can be combined to navigate competing fractional topological states.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates how engineering a superlattice on a Chern-insulator model can create a highly uniform miniband capable of hosting a fractional Chern insulator. By analyzing the competition between different correlated states using pseudospin anisotropy, the authors show a pathway to selectively control the ground state between a balanced FQSH-like state and a fully polarized FCI.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of engineering and controlling competing fractional topological states by combining band structure reconstruction, interaction-driven correlation effects, and external control mechanisms.
main_result:
The authors demonstrate that applying a superlattice modulation to the QWZ model creates a narrow miniband hosting a $
u=1/3$ Fractional Chern Insulator (FCI), which, when paired with its time-reversed partner (BHZ), exhibits a competition between a balanced FQSH-like state and a fully polarized FCI.
method: The study uses exact diagonalization on a projected interacting Hamiltonian derived from the superlattice-reconstructed single-particle band, supplemented by analysis of energy sector competition using pseudospin anisotropy.
model_or_system: The system is based on the Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) Chern-insulator model, modified by a scalar superlattice modulation to form a BHZ superlattice. The analysis focuses on the resulting isolated $C=+1$ miniband and its many-body physics at total filling $2/3$.
key_observables: Berry curvature ($\Omega$), quantum metric fluctuation ($\delta 	ext{Tr } g$), Chern number ($	ext{CMB}$), and the relative energies of competing polarization sectors ($E_P$).
important_parameters:
Total filling ($
u=2/3$), superlattice modulation strength ($V_0$), and the strength of the uniform pseudospin anisotropy ($g_z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the superlattice reconstruction successfully isolates the target miniband, and that the competition between states can be mapped onto the relative energy shifts governed by pseudospin anisotropy.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the superlattice reconstruction, showing the narrow, isolated target miniband and the reduction in geometric fluctuations. Figure 2 confirms the FCI nature via spectral flow and $	ext{CMB}=1$. Figure E1 details how uniform anisotropy shifts the energy of different polarization sectors, determining the ground state.
paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the physical model using a superlattice applied to the QWZ model. It then analyzes the single-particle reconstruction to confirm the formation of a uniform, isolated miniband. Subsequently, it performs many-body calculations to identify the $
u=1/3$ FCI, and finally, it analyzes the competition between different fractional states using the pseudospin anisotropy parameter.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, tunable lattice platform (superlattice) to realize and control multiple competing topological phases (FQSH vs. FCI), which is highly relevant for designing artificial quantum matter systems.
